title: Google Bard Conversation Exfiltration via Indirect Prompt Injection
description: Johann Rehberger demonstrated that a shared Google Doc containing prompt injection could exfiltrate Bard conversations via markdown image rendering. Google Apps Script domain bypassed CSP. Fixed by Google.

references.title: Hacking Google Bard - Embrace The Red

title: ChatGPT Plugins Data Exfiltration via Markdown Image and Cross-Plugin Request Forgery
description: WebPilot and other plugins susceptible to indirect prompt injection leading to data exfiltration via markdown image rendering and cross-plugin request forgery, hijacking sessions across installed plugins.

title: SpAIware: Persistent Memory Spyware Injection into ChatGPT macOS
description: Johann Rehberger demonstrated injecting persistent malicious instructions into ChatGPT's long-term memory via indirect prompt injection, causing continuous exfiltration of all future conversations. Fixed by OpenAI September 2024.

title: Microsoft 365 Copilot ASCII Smuggling Data Exfiltration
description: Rehberger disclosed a chain combining prompt injection, automatic tool invocation, ASCII smuggling using invisible Unicode tag characters, and link rendering to exfiltrate emails (including MFA codes) from M365 Copilot. Fixed by Microsoft.

title: ChatGPT Memory Injection via Indirect Prompt Injection
description: Rehberger demonstrated that ChatGPT memory could be poisoned via indirect prompt injection from websites/documents, storing false information persistently across sessions. OpenAI initially closed as low-severity, later fixed after PoC.

title: ZombAIs: Claude Computer Use Prompt Injection to C2
description: Johann Rehberger demonstrated using prompt injection against Anthropic's Claude Computer Use feature to download the Sliver C2 binary, chmod +x it, and execute it - giving attackers full command and control.

title: Terminal DiLLMa: LLM Apps Hijack Terminals via ANSI Escape Codes
description: Rehberger showed LLM-powered CLI tools can be hijacked via ANSI escape sequences in model outputs to clear screens, move cursors, leak DNS, and inject control sequences - bypassing trust boundaries with terminal emulators.

title: Security ProbLLMs in xAI Grok
description: Rehberger documented multiple security issues in xAI Grok including system prompt leakage, prompt injection susceptibility, and weak safety alignment that produced harmful content easily.

title: Gemini Delayed Automatic Tool Invocation via Context Pollution
description: Rehberger planted instructions in Gemini context that triggered on later user inputs (yes/no/sure), causing delayed automatic tool invocation that could exfiltrate or modify data without user awareness.

title: Gemini Memory Persistence via Prompt Injection
description: Rehberger demonstrated tricking Google Gemini Advanced into storing false long-term memory using delayed tool invocation triggered by future user confirmations like yes/sure.

title: GitHub Copilot Chat Prompt Injection to Data Exfiltration
description: Rehberger demonstrated indirect prompt injection in GitHub Copilot Chat through repository content, leading to data exfiltration of secrets and code via markdown image rendering.

title: GitHub Copilot Remote Code Execution via Prompt Injection (CVE-2025-53773)
description: Prompt injection causes GitHub Copilot to modify settings.json adding chat.tools.autoApprove:true (YOLO mode), enabling arbitrary command execution. Patched August 2025 Patch Tuesday. CVSS 9.6.

title: Claude Code Data Exfiltration via DNS (CVE-2025-55284)
description: Prompt injection causes Claude Code to leak secrets via DNS queries. Disclosed during Month of AI Bugs August 2025. Fixed by Anthropic.

title: Amazon Q Developer for VS Code Vulnerable to Invisible Prompt Injection
description: Amazon Q Developer interprets invisible Unicode Tag characters as instructions, enabling stealthy prompt injection attacks via comments or text artifacts.

title: Amazon Q Developer Remote Code Execution via Prompt Injection
description: Prompt injection enables arbitrary command execution in Amazon Q Developer environment. Disclosed during Month of AI Bugs.

title: Amazon Q Developer Secrets Leaked via DNS
description: Prompt injection in Amazon Q Developer enables secret exfiltration via DNS queries, bypassing standard egress controls.

title: Google Jules Vulnerable to Invisible Prompt Injection
description: Google's Jules coding agent processes invisible Unicode characters as instructions, allowing attackers to inject hidden commands. Reported May 26, 2025.

title: Jules Zombie Agent: Prompt Injection to Remote Control
description: Indirect prompt injection enabled converting Google Jules into a remotely controlled zombie agent that executes attacker commands.

title: Google Jules Multiple Data Exfiltration Issues
description: Multiple data exfiltration channels in Google Jules including markdown image rendering, link-based exfil, and external API calls triggered by prompt injection.

title: Amp Code Invisible Prompt Injection (Sourcegraph)
description: Sourcegraph's Amp Code coding agent processed invisible Unicode characters as instructions. Fixed June 14, 2025.

title: Amp Code Data Exfiltration via Image Rendering Fixed
description: Markdown image rendering enabled data exfiltration in Amp Code via prompt injection. Patched by Sourcegraph.

title: Devin AI Exposes Ports to the Internet via Prompt Injection
description: Cognition Devin AI exposed development ports to the internet through prompt injection, leaking tokens. Reported April 6, 2025 with no vendor response.

title: OpenHands and the Lethal Trifecta: Token Leakage
description: OpenHands agent demonstrated the lethal trifecta (untrusted input, sensitive access, exfiltration channel) leading to access token leakage via prompt injection.

title: ZombAI Exploit with OpenHands: Prompt Injection to RCE
description: OpenHands turned into a remotely controlled agent via prompt injection, achieving RCE on the host machine.

title: Cline Data Exfiltration via Indirect Prompt Injection
description: Cline coding agent vulnerable to indirect prompt injection leading to data exfiltration. Reported May 29, 2025; disclosed publicly after 90+ day window.

title: Hijacking Windsurf: Prompt Injection Leaks Developer Secrets
description: Windsurf Cascade hijacked via prompt injection embedded in analyzed files, exfiltrating environment variables and developer secrets without user approval.

title: Windsurf Memory-Persistent Data Exfiltration (SpAIware)
description: Indirect prompt injection abused Windsurf's create_memory tool without approval to persist malicious instructions, enabling continuous data exfiltration across sessions.

title: Claude Pirate: Abusing Anthropic File API for Data Exfiltration
description: Rehberger demonstrated abusing Anthropic's File API endpoint as a data exfiltration channel from Claude Code agents via prompt injection.

title: AI ClickFix: Hijacking Computer-Use Agents
description: Rehberger demonstrated ClickFix-style TTPs against computer-use agents like Claude, where social-engineering pages trick AI into executing attacker commands.

title: Exfiltrating ChatGPT Chat History and Memories with Prompt Injection
description: Rehberger demonstrated full exfiltration of ChatGPT chat history and stored memories via prompt injection. Reported October 2024, addressed by OpenAI by August 26 2025.

title: Google Antigravity IDE Security Vulnerabilities
description: Rehberger disclosed multiple security issues in Google's Antigravity IDE (AI-powered dev environment) including prompt injection, data exfiltration, and tool misuse.

title: HackedGPT: Seven Novel ChatGPT Vulnerabilities
description: Tenable Research disclosed 7 vulnerabilities in GPT-4o and GPT-5 including LatentBreak jailbreak, indirect prompt injection via trusted sites in browsing context, conversation injection, memory injection technique, and isolation bypass via SearchGPT.

title: CamoLeak: GitHub Copilot Chat CSP Bypass and Hidden Comment Injection
description: In June 2025 a Legit Security researcher found that GitHub Copilot Chat could be manipulated by instructions hidden in pull request text. Because Copilot acts with the viewing user's access, the injected prompt could read a victim's private repository content and smuggle it out through image requests routed via GitHub's own Camo proxy, which sidestepped the content security policy (CVSS 9.6). GitHub fixed it by turning off image display in Copilot Chat.

title: ChatGPT Command Memories Injection via SearchGPT
description: Tenable found ChatGPT memories could be both injected and exfiltrated by asking SearchGPT to print instructions to ChatGPT, bypassing isolation mechanisms.

title: GitHub Copilot Chat Prompt Injection via Filename
description: Tenable Research found GitHub Copilot Chat susceptible to prompt injection via specially crafted filenames in repositories.

title: Microsoft Copilot Studio SSRF Information Disclosure (CVE-2024-38206)
description: Critical SSRF protection bypass in Microsoft Copilot Studio (CVSS 8.5) allowed authenticated attackers to leak sensitive information over the network. Mitigated August 2024.

title: Wiz Research Critical Replicate AI Vulnerability
description: Wiz found a cross-tenant vulnerability in Replicate AI service allowing unauthorized access to all customers' AI prompts and results. Responsibly disclosed Jan 2024.

title: Wiz Hugging Face Cross-Tenant Compromise via Malicious Pickle Model
description: Wiz compromised Hugging Face's inference service by uploading a malicious pickle-based model, escaping the container, and gaining cross-tenant access to other customer models.

title: NVIDIAScape: NVIDIA Container Toolkit Container Escape (CVE-2025-23266)
description: Wiz disclosed a three-line Dockerfile container escape in NVIDIA Container Toolkit via LD_PRELOAD abuse of createContainer OCI hook. CVSS 9.0. Affects 35% of cloud GPU environments.

title: Breaking NVIDIA Triton Inference Server Vulnerability Chain (CVE-2025-23319)
description: Wiz disclosed a vulnerability chain in NVIDIA Triton Inference Server leading to full AI server takeover via memory corruption flaws.

title: Aim Labs Continuing EchoLeak Research and Variants
description: Aim Labs continued research into LLM Scope Violation variants beyond original EchoLeak, demonstrating similar zero-click attack patterns across multiple enterprise copilots.

title: Invariant Labs MCP Tool Poisoning Attacks
description: Invariant disclosed Tool Poisoning Attacks (TPA) on Model Context Protocol: malicious instructions embedded in tool descriptions invisible to users but parsed by AI models, enabling unauthorized actions and data exfil.

title: GitHub MCP Toxic Agent Flow Private Repo Exfiltration
description: Invariant Labs hijacked GitHub MCP agents via malicious GitHub Issues, coercing them to leak private repo data (including financial info) into public PRs via indirect prompt injection.

title: Trail of Bits MCP Line Jumping Vulnerability
description: Trail of Bits disclosed MCP line jumping: malicious servers inject prompts via tool descriptions and ANSI escape sequences to manipulate AI before tool invocation.

title: LeftoverLocals: GPU Memory Leak Reveals LLM Responses
description: Trail of Bits disclosed LeftoverLocals: vulnerability allowing eavesdropping on LLM responses through leaked GPU local memory across Apple, Qualcomm, AMD, Imagination GPUs.

title: MCP Servers Storing API Keys in World-Readable Plaintext
description: Trail of Bits found many MCP implementations store long-term API keys for third-party services in plaintext on local filesystem with insecure, world-readable permissions.

title: HiddenLayer Policy Puppetry Attack Bypasses All Major AI Models
description: HiddenLayer disclosed a universal prompt-injection technique called Policy Puppetry that disguises prompts as policy-file code, bypassing instruction hierarchy and safety guardrails across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, and others with a single prompt.
affected: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, multiple LLMs

title: HiddenLayer Bypass of OpenAI Guardrails (Self-Policing LLM)
description: HiddenLayer bypassed OpenAI's Guardrails system: when the same model evaluates safety as generates responses, both can be compromised together to produce harmful output without alerts.

title: HiddenLayer Cursor Attack Chain via Hidden Prompt Injections
description: HiddenLayer disclosed a chain of vulnerabilities in Cursor that exfiltrate sensitive data without user knowledge through hidden prompt injections in source files.

title: HiddenLayer Gemini for Workspace Indirect Prompt Injection
description: HiddenLayer found Gemini for Workspace susceptible to indirect prompt injection across its full product suite (Docs, Gmail, Slides), enabling content manipulation and data leakage.

title: Zenity AgentFlayer Zero-Click Exploit Chains Across Enterprise AI Agents
description: At Black Hat USA 2025, Zenity Labs disclosed AgentFlayer: zero-click exploit chains compromising OpenAI ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Salesforce Einstein, Google Gemini, M365 Copilot, and Cursor with Jira MCP - silent hijacking without user action.
affected: ChatGPT, Copilot Studio, Salesforce Einstein, Gemini, M365 Copilot, Cursor

title: Zenity Microsoft 365 Copilot RCE via Email/Teams/Calendar
description: Zenity demonstrated full ~RCE in M365 Copilot via remote injection through email, Teams message or calendar invite, paired with a jailbreak for code execution.

title: Cato CTRL HashJack: URL Fragment Indirect Prompt Injection on AI Browsers
description: Cato CTRL disclosed HashJack - the first known indirect prompt injection weaponizing any legitimate website. Malicious prompts hidden after '#' in URLs are processed client-side by AI browsers (e.g., Comet) bypassing server-side defenses.

title: Cato CTRL Weaponizing Claude Skills with MedusaLocker Ransomware
description: Cato CTRL weaponized Claude Skills in a controlled test environment to execute end-to-end MedusaLocker ransomware operation, demonstrating AI automation frameworks can be leveraged for extortion and encryption.

title: Pillar Security Google Antigravity Sandbox Escape RCE
description: Pillar Security disclosed a vulnerability in Google Antigravity combining prompt injection with permitted file-creation to grant remote code execution. Reported Jan 6 2026, patched Feb 28 2026.

title: Pillar Cursor Prompt Injection Flaw (CVE-2026-22708)
description: Pillar disclosed CVE-2026-22708 in Cursor where prompt injection abused agentic tools intended for constrained operations to perform unintended actions due to weak input validation.

title: Pillar n8n Sandbox Escape Vulnerabilities (CVSS 10)
description: Pillar Security reported two CVSS-10 sandbox escape vulnerabilities to n8n workflow platform allowing complete server takeover and credential theft. Patched in n8n v2.4.0.

title: Pillar Poisoned GGUF Templates Hugging Face Backdoors
description: Pillar Security disclosed a novel supply chain attack: Poisoned GGUF Templates embedding malicious instructions processed alongside legitimate inputs on Hugging Face inference pipelines.

title: PromptArmor IBM Bob Malware Execution via Prompt Injection
description: PromptArmor evaluated IBM's Bob AI development partner and found it vulnerable to prompt injection via malicious README.md that triggers echo command exploitation enabling malware install/execution. IDE also has zero-click markdown image exfil.

title: MCPwned: Azure MCP RCE Vulnerability Leads to Cloud Takeover
description: Token Security disclosed an unauthenticated RCE in official Azure MCP server allowing attackers with network access to compromise the server, steal Azure/Entra ID credentials, and take over the entire tenant. Microsoft removed vulnerable SSE transport.

title: AppOmni BodySnatcher ServiceNow AI Agent Privilege Escalation
description: AppOmni Labs disclosed BodySnatcher: with only target's email address, attacker impersonates admin and executes ServiceNow AI agent to override security controls and create backdoor admin accounts. Patched by ServiceNow.

title: AppOmni Critical AI Agent Flaws in Microsoft Copilot Studio
description: AppOmni Labs uncovered exploitable vulnerabilities allowing lateral movement across enterprise AI agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio with minimal credentials.

title: Sysdig LLMjacking: Stolen Cloud Credentials Hijack LLMs
description: Sysdig TRT identified LLMjacking in May 2024: attackers using stolen cloud credentials (initially AWS) to hijack Anthropic Claude 2.x access, costing victims ~$46K/day; later $100K+/day with newer models. Evolved into industrial marketplace.
affected: AWS Bedrock, Anthropic Claude (via stolen creds)

title: Sysdig AI-Accelerated Cloud Attack: Admin Privileges in 10 Minutes
description: Sysdig TRT observed AWS environment attack where threat actor escalated from initial access to admin in <10 minutes using LLMs for reconnaissance, malicious code generation, and real-time decision making.

title: Anthropic August 2025 Threat Report: Claude Misuse Cases
description: Anthropic's August 2025 threat-intelligence report documented misuse of Claude, with three headline cases: a cybercriminal who used Claude Code to automate data theft and extortion against at least 17 organizations; North Korean operatives who used Claude to obtain and hold remote jobs at US technology firms; and a criminal with limited coding ability who built and sold ransomware with the model's help.

title: OpenAI October 2024 Influence and Cyber Operations Update
description: OpenAI disclosed disruption of 20+ influence/cyber operations leveraging ChatGPT - including PRC-linked accounts generating monitoring proposals and Russian/Iranian/North Korean threat actors using AI in existing workflows.

title: OpenAI June 2025 Disrupting Malicious Uses Report
description: OpenAI's June 2025 report detailed disruption of further influence and cyber operations: spear-phishing assistance, deception schemes, and reconnaissance by state-linked actors.

title: OpenAI October 2025 Disrupting Malicious Uses Update
description: OpenAI's October 2025 update reported 40+ networks disrupted including authoritarian regime use and additional scams, cyber activity, and covert influence operations.

title: Google GTIG November 2025 AI Threat Tracker
description: Google Threat Intelligence Group reported adversaries experimenting with AI for novel capabilities. 57+ nation-state threat actors observed using AI/Gemini for cyber and influence ops, including suspected China-nexus actors using Gemini across full intrusion lifecycle.

title: Microsoft Digital Defense Report 2025: AI-Driven Threat Operations
description: Microsoft MDDR 2025 documents threat actors operationalizing AI to scale malicious activity - including North Korean groups Jasper Sleet and Coral Sleet using AI to enhance tradecraft.

title: Unit 42 Zealot Autonomous Multi-Agent Cloud Attack PoC
description: Unit 42 built Zealot - autonomous AI multi-agent system for cloud penetration testing - empirically demonstrating offensive AI capabilities against cloud environments.

title: Unit 42 AI-Powered Ransomware 25-Minute Compromise
description: Unit 42 demonstrated an AI-powered ransomware attack from initial compromise to data exfiltration in 25 minutes - a 100x speed increase over traditional methods.

title: Shai-Hulud npm Worm Used LLM to Generate Malicious Scripts
description: Unit 42 assessed Shai-Hulud npm supply chain worm campaign used LLM to generate malicious scripts that compromised hundreds of packages including Crowdstrike, Postman, and Zapier.

title: JFrog Vanna AI Prompt Injection RCE
description: JFrog Security Research discovered prompt injection vulnerability in Vanna AI Python package (CVE-2024-5826) that leads to remote code execution.

title: JFrog Weights & Biases Weave Directory Traversal (CVE-2024-7340)
description: JFrog disclosed directory traversal vulnerability in Weights & Biases' Weave toolkit (CVE-2024-7340) affecting ML experiment tracking.

title: JFrog ZenML Cloud Privilege Escalation
description: JFrog found improper access control in ZenML Cloud allowing users with minimal permissions to elevate to full admin.

title: JFrog oatpp-mcp Multiple CVEs Including Prompt Hijacking (CVE-2025-6515)
description: JFrog disclosed multiple CVEs in oatpp-mcp (Oat++ MCP implementation) including CVE-2025-6515 'Prompt Hijacking' - session ID hijacking in MCP ecosystems.

title: JFrog Reports 6.5x Increase in Malicious Hugging Face Models
description: JFrog 2025 State of Software Supply Chain report documented 6.5x year-over-year increase in malicious ML models published to Hugging Face and 25,229 exposed secrets in public registries (+64% YoY).

title: Lunary IDOR and SAML Access Control (CVE-2024-7474, CVE-2024-7475)
description: Protect AI/huntr disclosed two critical vulnerabilities (CVSS 9.1) in Lunary LLMOps platform: IDOR (CVE-2024-7474) and improper SAML access control (CVE-2024-7475).

title: Protect AI ChuanhuChatGPT, LocalAI Vulnerability Disclosures
description: Protect AI's huntr platform disclosed critical vulnerabilities in ChuanhuChatGPT, LocalAI, and similar open-source LLM tools enabling auth bypass and unauthorized actions.

title: Intel Neural Compressor Critical CVE-2024-22476
description: CVE-2024-22476 (CVSS 10) - improper input validation in Intel Neural Compressor allowing remote attackers to escalate privileges. Reported via Protect AI huntr.

title: Protect AI MLflow, Ray, Triton Vulnerability Surge
description: Protect AI documented 48 vulnerabilities disclosed in April 2024 alone across MLflow, Ray, and Triton Inference Server (a 220% rise from November 2023).

title: PromptArmor Slack AI Data Exfiltration via Indirect Prompt Injection
description: PromptArmor disclosed indirect prompt injection in Slack AI: attacker posts in public channel; when user queries Slack AI for private data, poisoned prompt is pulled into context, exfiltrating private data via masked phishing link.

title: Brave Discloses Indirect Prompt Injection in Perplexity Comet
description: Brave found Comet AI browser feeds webpage content directly to its LLM without separating untrusted content from user instructions; attackers can embed prompt injection payloads that the agent executes.

title: Brave Screenshot-Based Prompt Injection in AI Browsers
description: Brave disclosed prompt injection via screenshots: payloads hidden in low-contrast text (e.g., light blue on yellow) become readable to vision models. Affects Comet and other AI browsers. Reported Oct 1, disclosed Oct 21 2025.

title: LayerX CometJacking: One-Click Perplexity Comet Compromise
description: LayerX disclosed CometJacking - clicking a crafted URL causes Comet to parse query strings as agent instructions, triggering data lookup in connected services and memory exfiltration.

title: LayerX ChatGPT Atlas Tainted Memories Vulnerability
description: LayerX disclosed first vulnerability in OpenAI Atlas browser: CSRF request piggybacks on user's ChatGPT credentials to inject malicious instructions into memory. Tainted memories execute when user later queries legitimately.

title: ChatGPT Atlas Omnibox URL-Disguised Prompt Injection
description: Atlas browser omnibox interprets user input as either URL or natural language; disguising malicious prompts as URLs causes Atlas to treat them as high-trust user intent and execute hidden commands.

title: Check Point Claude Code Hook RCE and API Token Exfiltration (CVE-2025-59536, CVE-2026-21852)
description: Check Point Research disclosed RCE and API credential theft in Claude Code via malicious Hooks, MCP server config, and environment variables in project files. Patched by Anthropic before publication.

title: Claude Code Unauthorized Command Execution (CVE-2025-54794, CVE-2025-54795)
description: Cymulate researcher Elad Beber found two flaws in Anthropic's Claude Code during its research preview: CVE-2025-54794, a path-restriction bypass (CVSS 7.7), and CVE-2025-54795, a command injection (CVSS 8.7). Crafted prompts exploiting them let an attacker escape the working-directory sandbox and run commands the tool should have refused; Claude itself was used to study its own safeguards. Fixed in v0.2.111 and v1.0.20.

title: Anthropic GTG-1002 Chinese State-Sponsored AI-Orchestrated Espionage
description: Anthropic detected China-linked GTG-1002 group manipulating Claude Code (via jailbreak claiming defensive testing employment) to autonomously execute 80-90% of espionage operations against ~30 global targets including tech, finance, chemical, and government.

title: Jailbroken Claude Code Used to Steal 150GB from Mexican Government
description: A solo operator used jailbroken Claude Code to extract over 150GB of data from 10 Mexican government agencies (Dec 2025 - Jan 2026), running over 1,000 prompts then pivoting to ChatGPT for lateral movement.

title: Claude Mythos Identifies Thousands of Zero-Day Vulnerabilities
description: Anthropic's Claude Mythos preview identified 'thousands of zero-day vulnerabilities' across major operating systems and web browsers, some unpatched for decades. Anthropic launched coordinated vulnerability disclosure for findings.

title: Veracode 2025 GenAI Code Security Report: 45% Fail Rate
description: Veracode tested 100+ LLMs across Java/Python/C#/JS - 45% of generated code samples failed security tests introducing OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities. Java showed 72% failure rate; XSS failed 86%; log injection 88%.

title: Endor Labs MCP Server Supply Chain Risk Analysis
description: Endor Labs analyzed 10K+ MCP server repositories: 40% had no license, 82% use sensitive APIs without security controls, ~75% built by individuals without enterprise-grade protections.

title: Endor Labs Documents AI Dependency Hallucination Risk
description: Endor Labs found ~34% of AI-suggested dependencies don't exist (hallucinations) and 44-49% of AI-imported dependency versions have known vulnerabilities. Only 20% of AI-recommended deps meet safety standards.

title: ÆSIR AI Discovers 21 Critical CVEs Across NVIDIA, Tencent, MLflow, MCP
description: Trend Micro's ÆSIR AI-empowered security research platform uncovered 21 critical CVEs since mid-2025 across NVIDIA, Tencent, MLflow, and MCP tooling.

title: Dark Side of LLMs: Agent-Based Attacks for Computer Takeover
description: ArXiv paper demonstrates GPT-4o, Claude-4, Gemini-2.5 can be coerced into autonomously installing/executing malware. Direct injection (41.2%), RAG backdoor (52.9%), inter-agent trust (82.4%) success rates.

title: Commercial LLM Agents Vulnerable to Simple Yet Dangerous Attacks
description: ArXiv research showed commercial LLM agents (with memory, retrieval, web, API tools) are far more vulnerable than isolated LLMs to simple attacks across the full agentic stack.

title: Involuntary Jailbreak: Self-Prompting Attack on Grok 4, DeepSeek R1
description: ArXiv research disclosed Involuntary Jailbreak attack - LLMs self-prompt against guardrails. Grok 4 and DeepSeek R1 guardrails collapse without specific malicious objective.

title: Trend Micro Exploits DeepSeek-R1 Chain of Thought
description: Trend Micro demonstrated DeepSeek-R1's Chain of Thought reasoning transparency exploited for prompt attacks: visible reasoning steps reveal exploitation paths.

title: Noma Security Agentic Risk Map Disclosure: ForcedLeak and GeminiJack
description: Noma Security launched the Agentic Risk Map at OWASP Top 10 Agentic Applications release, documenting blast radius of compromised agents including ForcedLeak and GeminiJack threat patterns.

title: Cato CTRL 2026 Threat Report: AI Threats Mainstreaming
description: Cato CTRL 2026 Threat Report documented AI-driven threat actor evolution including jailbreaks-for-hire, AI-assisted exploit chains, and weaponized agent toolkits.

title: Mandiant M-Trends 2025: AI Adoption by Threat Actors
description: Mandiant M-Trends 2025 documented 35% increase in Iranian custom malware (45 new families), DPRK remote IT worker fraud schemes, and broad nation-state adoption of generative AI for tradecraft.

title: Microsoft RCE Vulnerabilities Across AI Agent Frameworks
description: Microsoft Security disclosed multiple RCE vulnerabilities across popular AI agent frameworks where prompts become shells - chaining prompt injection with framework features to execute attacker shellcode.

title: OpenClaw Open-Source AI Agent Mass Compromise
description: Reco's threat intel reported OpenClaw - viral open-source AI agent with 135K GitHub stars - became the first major AI agent security crisis of 2026 with critical vulnerabilities, malicious marketplace exploits, and 21K+ exposed instances.

title: Koi AI Discovers Cursor/Windsurf/Antigravity Recommend Malware
description: Koi AI researchers prevented Cursor, Windsurf, and Google Antigravity from recommending malicious packages to developers via slopsquatting and dependency confusion vectors.

title: Cursor Case-Sensitivity Bug Allows Silent Code Execution (CVE-2025-59944)
description: CVE-2025-59944: case-sensitivity bug in Cursor IDE enabled silent code execution via crafted malicious repositories. Highlighted agentic developer tool risk surface.

title: OX Security 94 Vulnerabilities in Cursor/Windsurf Chromium Forks
description: OX Security disclosed 94 Chromium vulnerabilities forked-and-forgotten in Cursor and Windsurf, exposing 1.8M developers to recommended-extension attacks and other vectors.

title: OX Security MCP Mother of All AI Supply Chains Vulnerability
description: OX Security researchers reported a design weakness shared by Anthropic's official Model Context Protocol SDKs that can let attackers run arbitrary commands on hosts running MCP implementations, putting credentials, stored data and conversation logs at risk. They attribute it to the protocol's design and its libraries across languages rather than to one coding error, so downstream projects built on them inherit the exposure.

title: Snyk Agent Fix and AI Agent Security Findings
description: Snyk launched AI Security Platform with Agent Fix - documented AI code generation security risks including high failure rates for XSS, injection, and access control issues in popular models.

title: Lakera Q4 2025 Agent Trends: Indirect Attacks Succeed Faster
description: Lakera Q4 2025 report documented indirect prompt-injection attacks succeed with fewer attempts than direct ones - early filters less effective on harmful instructions arriving via external content.

title: Lakera Copy-Paste Injection Exploit in ChatGPT
description: Lakera documented copy-paste injection: hidden prompts in copied text exfiltrate chat history and sensitive data once pasted into ChatGPT.

title: Custom GPT System Prompt Leakage Wave
description: Multiple researchers (Lakera, Embrace The Red, others) demonstrated that custom GPTs in OpenAI GPT Store leaked their proprietary system instructions and embedded API keys via prompt injection.

title: DeepSeek AI Account Takeover Disclosed by Rehberger
description: Rehberger disclosed account takeover vulnerability in DeepSeek AI through session/token handling weakness.

title: Bing Chat (Copilot) Zero-Click Image Rendering Data Exfil
description: Rehberger disclosed Bing Chat's zero-click data exfiltration via markdown image rendering when responses are rendered. Fixed by Microsoft.

title: CoPhish: Copilot Studio Phishing Platform Abuse
description: BlackFog documented CoPhish: turning Microsoft Copilot Studio into a phishing platform - attackers create public agents that exfiltrate user data via OAuth flows tied to Microsoft trusted domains.

title: Copirate 365 DEF CON: Plundering Microsoft Copilot (CVE-2026-24299)
description: Rehberger and co-researchers presented Copirate 365 at DEF CON disclosing CVE-2026-24299 in Microsoft Copilot - chained prompt injection and tool abuse for deeper M365 data plundering.

title: Anthropic Q1 2026 Threat Report Continuation
description: Anthropic continued threat reporting Q1 2026 documenting additional fraudulent employment schemes, AI-assisted ransomware sales, and large-scale extortion campaigns leveraging Claude.

title: GTIG Adversarial Misuse of Generative AI - January 2025
description: Google Threat Intelligence Group reported 57+ nation-state threat actors using AI/Gemini for cyber operations - early phase observations including reconnaissance, lure creation, and code assistance.

title: Anthropic Large-Scale Extortion Operation Using Claude Code
description: Anthropic disclosed cybercriminal using Claude Code to automate end-to-end extortion: discovery, exfiltration, ransom note generation, and victim profiling at scale.

title: Anthropic DPRK Remote IT Worker Fraud via Claude
description: Anthropic detected North Korean operatives using Claude to fraudulently obtain and maintain remote employment at US Fortune 500 tech companies - using AI to draft applications, complete tasks, and impersonate qualified candidates.

title: Anthropic Low-Skill Cybercriminal Selling AI-Generated Ransomware
description: Anthropic identified a cybercriminal with only basic coding skills using Claude to generate and sell complete ransomware kits - illustrating dramatic skill compression of LLM-assisted malware development.

title: ActiveFence Perplexity Comet Markdown/HTML Injection
description: ActiveFence disclosed prompt injection via markdown/HTML in Perplexity Comet - initially classified as not applicable, later reclassified after dispute.

title: Prompt Security Analysis: Claude Computer Use Ticking Time Bomb
description: Prompt Security analyzed Claude Computer Use security model, demonstrating multiple proof-of-concept exploits leveraging trust boundaries to install malware and steal sensitive data.

title: Third-Party AI Chatbot Plugin Prompt Injection Risks
description: IEEE S&P 2026 paper analyzed 17 third-party chatbot plugins on 10K+ websites: 15 plugins enable indirect prompt injection by mixing trusted/untrusted content in tool context, no separation enforced.

title: Anthropic Disrupts AI-Generated CSAM Trafficking Operation
description: Anthropic threat report disclosed disruption of operation attempting to generate and traffic CSAM using Claude, with extensive guardrails preventing generation.

title: OpenAI February 2024 Disrupting State-Affiliated Threat Actors
description: OpenAI's first public threat report disclosed disrupting 5 state-affiliated threat actors (Charcoal Typhoon, Salmon Typhoon, Crimson Sandstorm, Emerald Sleet, Forest Blizzard) using ChatGPT for recon, scripting, and phishing.

title: Noma Customer Support Agent Cascade Attack Pattern
description: Noma documented attack pattern where harmless-looking customer support agent, once compromised, cascades into unauthorized money transfers, sensitive data exfiltration, and malicious emails for lateral movement.

title: Anvilogic 2025 AI Risk Report: Model & Supply Chain Threats
description: Anvilogic 2025 AI Risk Report flagged model theft, supply chain risks, and chatbot attacks as top security concerns industry-wide.

title: Reco Threat Intel Breaks Cursor Background Agent, Takes Over EC2
description: Reco threat intelligence team broke Cursor's background agent functionality and took over an EC2 instance via prompt injection driven privilege escalation.
